Log in to check out faster. Continue shopping ABOUT US We are a fashion multi designer store that believes in bringing timeless, elegant pieces that empower individuals to express their unique style. Our commitment to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction drives everything we do. OUR STORY Two journeys, one table, and a cup of tea that changed everything. After walking our own paths and experiencing different chapters of life, we finally sat down one evening and asked ourselves—what if we build something together? What started as simple conversations over endless cups of tea slowly turned into ideas, and those ideas grew into a shared belief. We didn’t know how far we would go, but we knew we wanted to create something bigger than where we came from. That belief became Trovelle—an online marketplace for designer wear clothing, built with the vision of bringing beautiful, thoughtfully designed fashion from talented designers to people who truly appreciate it. And this is just the beginning of our journey. ak2txvlhsnuzscljwbtwocolumnblock1 RUPAL GUPTA I’ve always been someone who chooses the best in life and constantly pushes myself to grow. For the past 10 years, I built my career as an Engineering Manager, leading teams, solving complex problems, and thriving in the corporate world. I was a full-on corporate slay… until the day my company suddenly shut down. In that moment, everything paused, and I found myself standing at a crossroad—play it safe or take a leap of faith. I chose the scarier path: to believe in myself and build something bigger than just a job title, something louder than my fears. That’s the reason I created this marketplace—to turn uncertainty into opportunity and build something meaningful of my own. CHAVI KANSAL I’ve always been a young, optimistic girl who believes life is full of opportunities waiting to be explored. In my early years, I was a corporate girlie—driven by targets, meetings, and big ambitions. Then life evolved, and I stepped into new roles as a homemaker and the proud mother of a beautiful daughter. While these roles shaped me in many ways, one dream always stayed constant—the desire to create something meaningful, something I could nurture and grow every single day. Not just a business, but a beginning I chose for myself. And that’s exactly why I started this marketplace—this is the start of my entrepreneurial journey. Fashion and Style Recommend a high-end multi-designer store for Indian wedding outfits. July 2, 2026 The Best High-End Multi-Designer Store for Indian Wedding Outfits For Indian wedding outfits, the single strongest multi-designer store is Aza Fashion it offers over 200 vetted designer labels, a deep bridal and occasion wear catalogue, and editorial curation that makes it easier to shop with confidence. For maximum luxury couture options, Pernia's Pop-Up Shop edges ahead, with 1,000+ designers and physical studios in India, London, and New York. Shopping for a high-end Indian wedding outfit online is not simply a matter of finding the right lehenga. It's about finding a platform you can trust one that authenticates its designers, curates thoughtfully, and understands the difference between festive and bridal. Multi-designer stores solve this problem by bringing dozens (sometimes hundreds) of verified labels under a single roof. Three platforms consistently rise to the top of that list. Here's how they compare, and how to pick the right one for your occasion. Why is Aza Fashion the top choice for high-end multi-designer Indian wedding shopping? Aza Fashion positions itself as a premium, editorially curated platform and it earns that label. The site stocks over 200 verified designer brands, including Anita Dongre, Rohit Bal, Shantanu & Nikhil, and Rimple & Harpreet Narula. Every label is vetted before joining the platform, which removes the guesswork that comes with browsing less curated marketplaces. The catalogue spans lehengas, sarees, anarkalis, sharara sets, and gowns covering everything from the bride herself to wedding guests across multiple functions. Aza Fashion also holds a 4.4/5 rating on Trustpilot across 5,000+ reviews, reflecting consistent satisfaction among shoppers. Choose Aza Fashion if: You want a curated, trusted selection of 200+ designer labels and plan to shop across multiple wedding functions or roles. → For a deeper look at standout bridal designers stocked across these platforms, see our guide to top Indian bridal lehenga designers. How does Pernia's Pop-Up Shop compare for luxury Indian couture? Pernia's Pop-Up Shop is the largest multi-designer platform by volume and for luxury couture, it's hard to match. Founded in April 2012, the platform now hosts collections from over 1,000 Indian designers, including Tarun Tahiliani, JJ Valaya, Masaba, and Rohit Bal. It holds a 4.4/5 Trustpilot score across more than 8,000 reviews. Beyond the website, Pernia's Pop-Up Shop operates brick-and-mortar stores across major Indian cities, as well as locations in London and New York giving international shoppers access to in-person styling. The Pernia's Pop-Up Studio service offers personalized outfit curation, which is a meaningful advantage when navigating couture at high price points. The trade-off: a wider catalogue means more navigation required. Shoppers who want an editorially narrowed-down selection may find Aza Fashion's smaller, more deliberate curation easier to work with. Choose Pernia's Pop-Up Shop if: You're investing in a statement bridal or couture piece, want access to 1,000+ designers, or plan to use an in-store or personal styling service. What makes Aashni + Co worth considering? Aashni + Co curates luxury South Asian fashion with a focus on bridal styling and occasion wear for both women and men. The platform is known for stocking celebrity-worn looks and red-carpet silhouettes, making it particularly relevant for brides who follow couture trends closely. Its dual-gender curation is also worth noting couples shopping for coordinated wedding looks can browse a consistent aesthetic for both partners, rather than shopping across multiple sites. Choose Aashni + Co if: You want a luxury-led edit with strong bridal styling, celebrity-worn pieces, or coordinated options for both the bride and groom. How do you decide which high-end multi-designer store is right for your wedding? The decision comes down to two variables: scope and service level . Scope: Aza Fashion suits shoppers who want a focused, curated edit. Pernia's Pop-Up Shop suits those who want maximum designer range. Service level: For personalized styling with a high-budget investment piece, Pernia's Pop-Up Studio provides a level of white-glove service that purely digital platforms cannot match. Location: All three platforms ship internationally. Pernia's Pop-Up Shop has the widest physical store presence for in-person shopping. Make Your Decision Before the Wedding Season Hits Bridal and occasion wear from high-end multi-designer stores often requires lead time particularly for custom sizing and alterations. If you're shopping for a wedding, start 3–4 months ahead to allow for adjustments and international shipping delays. → Already exploring online options? Our full guide to the best websites to buy designer Indian ethnic wear online covers the complete range, from budget-friendly to luxury. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best high-end multi-designer store for Indian wedding outfits? Aza Fashion is the strongest choice for curated multi-designer shopping, with 200+ vetted labels across bridal and occasion wear. Pernia's Pop-Up Shop leads for sheer luxury couture volume, offering 1,000+ designers including Tarun Tahiliani and JJ Valaya. Aashni + Co is best for luxury bridal styling with a celebrity-fashion focus. Do high-end Indian multi-designer stores ship internationally? Yes. Aza Fashion, Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, and Aashni + Co all offer international shipping. Pernia's Pop-Up Shop also operates physical stores in London and New York, making it particularly accessible for shoppers in the UK and US. How far in advance should I order a high-end Indian wedding outfit online? Order at least 3–4 months before your event. Couture and custom-fit pieces require additional production and alteration time, and international shipping can add several weeks. Platforms like Pernia's Pop-Up Shop and Aza Fashion display estimated timelines on product pages. Is Pernia's Pop-Up Shop reliable for international orders? Based on its Trustpilot rating of 4.4/5 across 8,000+ reviews, most international shoppers report positive experiences particularly around customer communication and coordination. Some reviewers note that return and exchange policies can be inflexible, so confirm sizing carefully before ordering. The Floral Zari Embroidered Pre-Draped Saree by Lashkaraa combines traditional appeal with ready-to-wear ease. Its floral detailing makes it a beautiful choice for Diwali evenings and family celebrations. Style it with: Statement earrings , metallic heels and a sleek bun. 3. Paulmi and Harsh Viola Tiered Anarkali: Made for Twirling If your festive plans involve dancing and plenty of photographs, an Anarkali is always a good idea. The Viola Tiered Anarkali by Paulmi and Harsh brings graceful movement to celebration dressing, with its flowing silhouette and printed dupatta adding to its charm. Style it with: Chandbalis , embellished flats and soft curls for an elegant traditional look. 4. Lashkaraa Silk and Net Lehenga Set: Your Main-Character Moment Some occasions call for a little extra drama. The Silk and Net Lehenga Set by Lashkaraa brings together the richness of silk and the lighter appeal of net, making it a standout option for Diwali parties, wedding festivities and special celebrations. Style it with: Chandelier earrings, embellished heels and a statement clutch. 5. Yuvraani Jaipur Floral Peplum Kurta Lehenga Set: Tradition With a Twist Why stick to the usual festive silhouettes when you can switch things up? The Floral Peplum Kurta Lehenga Set by Yuvraani Jaipur combines a contemporary peplum shape with the celebratory appeal of a lehenga, making it perfect for festive gatherings and family functions. Style it with: Floral-inspired earrings, embroidered juttis and a delicate potli. 6. Style it with: Statement earrings, a sleek bun and strappy heels. Style it with: Statement earrings, a sleek bun and strappy heels. 7. Masaba Tropical Print Shirt and Skirt Set: Festive, but Make It Fun Not every celebration calls for a heavily embroidered lehenga. The Tropical Print Shirt and Skirt Set by Masaba brings a playful, fashion-forward mood to festive dressing, making it ideal for Diwali brunches, house parties and celebrations with friends. Style it with: Sculptural earrings, strappy heels and a metallic clutch. 8. Two Sisters by Gyans Mirror Work Peplum Top and Dhoti Pant Set: Let It Shine Mirror work, a statement-making peplum top and dhoti pants make this set a fun alternative to conventional festive wear. The Two Sisters by Gyans outfit brings traditional embellishment into a contemporary silhouette, perfect for festive evenings when you want to stand out. Style it with: Oxidised silver earrings , stacked bangles and metallic heels. 9. Saanjh by Lea Zaria Mashru Banarasi Silk Corset and Saree Set: The Saree, Reimagined Traditional Banarasi silk meets contemporary styling in the Zaria Mashru Banarasi Silk Corset and Saree Set by Saanjh by Lea . It is an elegant way to experiment with the corset trend while keeping the timeless appeal of Indian occasionwear intact. Style it with: A sleek bun, statement earrings and a compact evening clutch. 10. Renee Label Payalia Woven Saree: A Timeless Favourite A woven saree is one of those wardrobe staples that never needs much convincing. The Payalia Woven Saree by Renee Label is a versatile choice for festive pujas, family gatherings and intimate celebrations, with plenty of room to experiment with your styling. Over 25 years in the public eye, the cover star has questioned the definitions handed to her, from beauty and womanhood to sustainability and success. Today, she embraces complexity, chooses agency and finds freedom in allowing every facet of herself to coexist. Read along as she speaks about the roles she is looking forward to taking on, what she misses about old Bollywood, her relationship with age, and more in this candid conversation with Aza. Start Reading → Krithi Shetty With nearly a decade of experience at just 22, Krithi Shetty holds a quiet yet commanding presence in today’s attention economy. Her evolution has shaped not just a career, but a distinctly personal brand. The brand that is Krithi Shetty emerges as a blend of passion, tenacity and vulnerability. As our April cover star, she opens up about navigating online hate, the grounding force of familial support, and more. Start Reading → Jonita A woman of multiplicity, this fresh face with fierce vocals has effortlessly moved across cultures, genres and creative avenues. But that’s not all that makes Jonita cool. Reflecting on the experiences that continue to shape her voice and her identity as an artist, the pop queen speaks of her evolving musical ambitions, the unromantic realities of performance, her “pinch me” moment, and much more. Start Reading → Randeep Hooda In a league of his own, Randeep Hooda embraces a unique duality — the proper gentleman who could just as easily belong to the wilderness in another universe; the artist drawn to both Bollywood masala and Hollywood depth; the groom whose traditional Manipuri wedding was equal parts mischief and cultural rootedness. This International Men’s Day, we’re celebrating a man of range, restraint, and quiet intensity. Read the full Aza exclusive to dive deeper. Start Reading → Chitrangda Singh Since the inception of her career, Chitrangda Singh has stood tall in her truth: a woman who owns her narrative—whether it’s defying beauty norms, rewriting industry timelines or making bold creative choices. From tackling colourism in the modelling world to embracing motherhood as her most beautiful season, she’s proof that strength and softness can coexist. In this Aza exclusive, she speaks candidly of the moments that have shaped her, Indian representation on the global stage, her unique hobbies and much more. Start Reading → Uorfi Javed The rules have changed now that Uorfi is playing. As the queen of this game called fame, she has a love-hate relationship with the internet. The same platform that once criticized her fashion choices now applauds her guts and creativity. While Uorfi’s career trajectory makes a compelling case study on self-branding, Aza is digging deeper. In this unfiltered conversation, Uorfi opens up about her worldview, her abusive childhood, and offers a little peek into her romantic life among other topics. Start Reading → Pratibha Ranta A filmmaking course in Mumbai was this small-town beauty's ticket to the movies. Cut to 2024, Pratibha Ranta boasts two megahits on the opposite ends of cinematic experiences; a Sanjay Leela Bhansali larger-than-life period drama and an Aamir Khan and Kiran Rao production rooted in realism. One could argue that she brings her Midas touch to the table - but a deeper understanding of her passion and process tells us she's worked hard to be this versatile talent. In this exclusive interview with Aza, the fresh face talks about her progressive upbringing, the controversy surrounding Laapata Ladies' being India's entry to the Oscars, her preparation for the roles and much more. Start Reading → Dhvani Bhanushali India’s pop culture holy trinity—Bollywood, cricket, and music—has long shaped the nation’s identity. As a singer, our cover star is redefining the pop music scene with her idiosyncratic songs and tale-telling music videos. In this candid conversation with Dhvani Bhanushali, we go beyond the stage to delve into the making of a pop star and the singer's personal journey. From cardio singing and her backup plans to dream collaborations, the artist behind the chart-topping single, Vaaste reveals it all. Many years have passed since her breakthrough, and she remains on an evolving quest to find herself and her sound. But one thing is for sure, she keeps doing a damn good job. Start Reading → Taha Shah Badussha For the longest time, he was that guy you've seen somewhere but you can't place where. Now, he is Taha Shah Badussha, talented actor whose stellar performance as Tajdar in Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Heeramandi has made him suddenly ubiquitous (for all the right reasons). After 15 long years, the hidden gem got the break of his career, and yet the same zest continues to drive him today. Read along as our hot (pun intended) cover star shares what he looks for in his ideal partner, his fun interaction at Cannes Film Festival, and all he does to keep growing - over an energetic cover shoot with Aza. Start Reading → Alaviaa Jaaferi There’s much more to this “star kid” than her famous lineage. She is unafraid, self-assured and determined to chart her own course in the world of fashion. When Prime Video released its content lineup, the preview of her upcoming show, The Tribe , had everyone talking. While the show offers a glimpse into the life of Alaviaa Jaaferi, the influencer with a mission, we’re taking you inside the life of Alaviaa Jaaferi, the entrepreneur and daughter of Bollywood’s comedy legend, Jaaved Jaaferi (and it’s not what you’d expect). Join us as our muse divulges details about her upbringing, her fashion brand, her unique beauty tips and more in an exclusive conversation with Aza. Start Reading → Jasmine Bhasin A big scoop of hard work, a generous pinch of likable authenticity, and a sprinkle of good luck have created the phenomenon that is Jasmine Bhasin. Rising from the ranks to become the darling of Punjabi cinema today, our muse embarked on her journey to independence at a very young age, when she left her hometown of Kota to pursue a career in hospitality. She was discovered at her very first front desk job – crafting a perfect narrative of serendipity. Since then, she has consistently won hearts, emerging as the people's choice. In an intimate conversation with Aza, Jasmine delves into the details of her journey, recounts her most memorable fan encounter, shares insights into future plans, and much more. Now, with her multi-starrer action thriller Toxic set for release and the first Salim Siblings Productions film, Baby Do Die Do , earning critical acclaim, the powerhouse performer is evolving with the times while expanding her creative horizons. While this is the story of our cover star’s becoming, one thing remains unchanged: her purpose. For Huma, the craft has always come first, and the spotlight simply followed. Read on as she opens up about the emotional cost of being an actor, her dream wedding and much more. Also in this issue: your ultimate guide to building a celebration wardrobe, monsoon must-haves for every occasion, outfits chosen just as the stars intended, and the latest trends for your fashion-forward tribe. Start Reading → Shilpa Shetty Kundra When two emblems of enduring beauty—one, the timeless saree, and the other, our cover star—come together, the result is an extraordinary capsule that celebrates individuality and fierce femininity. In collaboration with the multifaceted Shilpa Shetty Kundra, Aza proudly unveils ROAR, a collection that balances softness with strength through its distinctive design. Our muse has always been a nonconformist—an original in style, fitness, and business. This capsule is a testament to that trailblazing spirit and her singular journey. Inside, she reflects on her first tryst with the saree, filming in the ’90s, and her relationship with Raj Kundra. Also featured: a curated edit of luxe essentials with Araiya by Aza, and a bridal glow manual from wellness entrepreneur and face yogi Vibhuti Arora. Marking Aza’s 20th anniversary, this special edition is both a celebration of our legacy and a glimpse into the future—one you do not want to miss. Start Reading → Women's Day Special For this first-of-a-kind issue, four extraordinary Indian-origin women from the west join hands with Aza to celebrate female power and create a space for authentic cultural representation. The Desi Big sister Ami Desai—with years of journalistic experience and expertise in beauty & lifestyle—takes the lead on the story. Her intention remains to highlight the ingenuity employed by fellow cover stars in redefining community, success and representation in the digital world. Also in this issue: Introducing Araiya by Aza , the future of fine jewellery; a curated selection of the season’s finest jackets for the groom and his entourage; and an exploration of themes in home décor, drawing parallels between apparel and interior design trends. Start Reading → Back and Better Six years after Aza and Mouni Roy first teamed up for a cover shoot, the Bengali beauty reflects on her journey, sharing insights into life after Brahmāstra and details of her dreamy nuptials to Suraj Nambiar. In this candid tête-à-tête, she also offers a glimpse into her inner world, discussing her diverse interests. Also in the magazine: the glitz and glamour of the Aza Ahmedabad store launch party, featuring a memorable shoot with inspiring women from the city, expert advice from bridal stylists on pressing issues faced by brides-to-be, a curated list of 2024 wedding trends, and more. Start Reading → The 'It' Girl Diana Penty’s journey began as an ingénue in her debut film. Since then, she has continued pushing boundaries, as is evident in her diverse movie choices such as Happy Bhag Jayegi and Parmanu: The Story of Pokhran . And that’s not all for our cover star! She has also impressed the audience and fashion critics with her recent appearances at the Cannes Film Festival and Paris Haute Couture Week. In a candid conversation with Aza, the stunner opens up about her evolution in the entertainment industry, her childhood aspirations, her upcoming projects alongside Bollywood bigwigs, and much more. Also in the magazine: Aza lists celebrity brides who wore wedding charms unique to them and those who hosted their nuptials in the intimate embrace of their homes. Do check out our curated selection of artsy accessories that will help you stand out this festive season! Start Reading → The Besties Edit In a tête-à-tête sprinkled with childhood anecdotes, actor-sister duo Kajal and Nisha Aggarwal open up to Aza on their unique bond, the need for self-love, motherhood, and more. Also in the magazine: Aza lists celeb-approved wedding gurus you cannot go wrong with. For all soon-to-weds manifesting a bridal entry like Kiara Advani on her wedding day, we have a compilation of soundtracks that have our heart. Do check out the summer must-haves from azafashions.com – we have curated everything from vibrant accessories to home décor pieces! Start Reading → The Celebration Issue Shriya Saran is in a happy space. The actor’s last project, Drishyam 2 entered the 200-crore club, she has a pan-India film Kabzaa lined up for release. And in conversation with Aza, Shriya revealed she’s working on a children’s apparel line – an ode to her daughter, Radha. For obvious reasons, the actor is an apt muse for Aza’s Celebration Issue. Do sift through the Aza X Celebrity Lookbook as we revisit our cover shoots of 2022, featuring global influencers and noted names in Indian cinema. Take our word for it – the best is yet to come! She follows her heart and how! And for that, it was a no-brainer for us to choose the actor as our muse for Aza’s Happiness Issue. In conversation with Aza, Nushrratt opens up on cinema, relationships and more. But a stunning lehenga can lose its shine fast if the accessories fight for attention instead of working with it. The secret isn't piling on more jewellery . It's choosing pieces that complement your lehenga's neckline, fabric and colour story so the whole look feels intentional. Here's how to accessorise a lehenga the right way this festive season. Let Your Neckline Guide Your Jewellery Your blouse neckline is the first decision point, and it's often the one people skip. A deep V-neck or sweetheart neckline looks beautiful with a statement necklace that fills the space. A high neckline or heavily embroidered collar, on the other hand, already does the talking, so a pair of earrings is usually enough. Think of the neckline as the frame, and your jewellery as what goes inside it. Match the two, and you're already halfway to a well-styled look. Statement Earrings or a Layered Necklace? This is the classic festive dilemma, and the answer comes down to proportion. If your lehenga has a busy neckline or heavy embellishment on the blouse, go with statement earrings, think chandbalis, jhumkas or polki drops, and skip the necklace altogether. If your blouse is simpler, a layered necklace in kundan or polki can become the centrepiece of your look, paired with smaller studs or jhumkis. A good rule for Diwali lehenga styling : pick one hero piece. Let it do the heavy lifting while everything else plays a supporting role. Gold vs Silver: Choosing the Right Jewellery Gold tends to suit warmer lehenga shades like maroon, rust, deep orange and gold embroidery, giving the outfit a traditional, festive warmth. Silver and oxidised jewellery work beautifully with cooler tones like emerald, royal blue, and pastel lehengas, lending a more contemporary edge. Polki and kundan jewellery sit somewhere in between. Both have a timeless, regal quality that works across most colour palettes, which is why they remain festive jewellery staples year after year. If you're unsure which to pick, check the undertone of your lehenga's embroidery thread. It usually points you in the right direction. How to Style Heavy and Minimal Lehengas A heavily embellished lehenga, think dense zardozi, sequins or mirror work, already carries visual weight. Here, less jewellery goes further. A pair of simple studs, a few delicate bangles and a well-chosen potli are often all you need. A minimal lehenga, by contrast, gives you room to play. This is where a layered necklace, stacked bangles or a cocktail ring can step in and add drama without overwhelming the outfit. Think of your lehenga's embellishment level as a budget. Spend it wisely across either the outfit or the jewellery, not both. The Finishing Touches: Potlis , Footwear and Hair Accessories The smaller details are what elevate a look from nice to memorable. An embellished potli in a matching or contrasting metallic tone works as both a functional and decorative piece. Footwear should echo the formality of the occasion, think embroidered juttis , kolhapuris with a festive twist, or heels with subtle embellishment. Hair accessories are often overlooked, but a maang tikka, a jadau hairpin or even fresh flowers can tie the whole look together, especially if your earrings are the statement piece and you want to balance the face frame. Colour -Coordinating Your Lehenga and Accessories You don't need an exact colour match between your lehenga and jewellery, but you do need a dialogue between them. Pick one or two colours from your lehenga's embroidery and let your jewellery, potli or footwear echo them. A green lehenga with gold thread work, for example, pairs beautifully with gold-toned jewellery with small emerald or green accents, rather than jewellery in an entirely unrelated colour. This is one of the simplest ways to make an outfit look curated rather than thrown together at the last minute. Finding the Right Balance for Your Festive Look The art of how to accessorise a lehenga really comes down to restraint. Choose a hero piece, keep your metal tones consistent, and let your neckline and embellishment level guide the rest. A well-balanced festive look isn't about how much jewellery you're wearing. It's about how well each piece earns its place. That version hasn't aged particularly well. But the wedge heel making its way back into rotation right now looks nothing like its predecessor. Think slimmer profiles, cleaner lines, and shapes that feel sculptural rather than stacked. This shift isn't about nostalgia. It's about designers rethinking what a wedge can be when you strip away the bulk and focus on proportion. The result is a shoe that works just as well with a linen suit as it does with a slip dress, and that's exactly why wedge heels are in style in 2026. Here are nine wedge heel styles worth knowing, plus how to wear them without looking like you raided a 2012 lookbook. Sculptural and Architectural Wedges These are the wedges doing the most visual work. Think curved heels, cutout midsoles, and shapes that look more like modern art than footwear. Designers are treating the wedge as a canvas, carving negative space into the base or angling it asymmetrically so the shoe reads as a statement piece on its own. Choose this style if you want your shoes to function as the outfit's focal point rather than a supporting detail. Wedge Flip-Flops The humble flip-flop has been quietly elevated. A wedge sole turns the most casual summer shoe into something with actual structure, often paired with leather straps or metallic hardware instead of basic rubber. They work best when you want comfort without sacrificing polish, think beach-to-dinner versatility. Thong Wedges Similar in spirit to flip-flops but dressier, thong wedges feature a single strap between the toes paired with a more refined wedge base, often in woven leather or smooth suede. They sit at the intersection of casual and elevated, which is part of why they've become a go -to for warm-weather dressing. Espadrille Wedges The espadrille wedge never fully disappeared, but it's been refined. Instead of the thick jute stacks from a decade ago, newer versions use a slimmer rope base paired with sleeker uppers in canvas, suede, or leather. Choose espadrille wedges if you want that effortless, European-summer feel without looking overly casual. Natural-Texture Wedges Jute and cork wedges remain a warm-weather staple, but the finishes are getting more intentional. Instead of rough, uniform texture, designers are mixing cork with smooth leather straps or pairing jute with unexpected colors, giving the natural material a more considered, less rustic feel. Wedge Sneakers Yes, sneaker wedges are back, but not in their bulky Isabel Marant era form. The 2026 version is lower, sleeker, and often disguised enough that you'd need a second glance to notice the hidden lift. These work well for anyone who wants height without committing to an obvious heel. Printed or Graphic Wedges Patterned wedges, whether animal print, abstract graphics, or bold color-blocking, are having a moment because they let the shoe do the talking in an otherwise simple outfit. A graphic wedge paired with a plain linen dress instantly elevates the whole look. Metallic Wedges Metallic finishes in silver, gold, or pewter are showing up across multiple wedge silhouettes this year. They photograph well, transition easily from day to night, and add a bit of shine without the commitment of a full sequin moment. Kolhapuri Wedges A modern take on traditional Indian foo t wear , Kolhapuri wedges pair signature braided straps and handcrafted details with the added height of a wedge heel. Style them with flowy kurtas, festive co- ords , or breezy maxi dresses for a contemporary ethnic look. How to Style Wedge Heels in 2026 The key to wearing trending wedge heels well comes down to proportion. Pair a chunkier wedge with something slim, like a fitted slip dress or straight-leg trousers, so the shoe doesn't compete with bulky fabric. On flowy maxi dresses, a sculptural or metallic wedge adds just enough edge to keep the look from feeling too soft. For tailored co-ords, a sleek wedge sneaker or architectural heel bridges casual and polished without overdoing it. And with linen trousers or relaxed summer separates, natural-texture or espadrille wedges feel intentional rather than mismatched. Choose woven textures and earthy tones if you're going for an easy, warm-weather look. Opt for metallics or graphic prints if you want your shoes to carry the outfit. If you're exploring designer footwear options to build out a full wardrobe around this trend, platforms like Aza make it easy to compare styles side by side and find pieces that fit your specific aesthetic. The Takeaway Wedge heel trends in 2026 prove that a shoe can come back around without feeling dated. The difference lies entirely in execution: sleeker proportions, better materials, and shapes that feel deliberate instead of accidental. Whether you gravitate toward a minimalist platform thong or a bold graphic print, there's a modern wedge heel style built for how you actually dress now. Designers from across the country converged to present collections that bridge traditional heritage with forward-thinking fashion. This season emphasi s ed sustainability, bold structural silhouettes, and modern luxury pret. From star-studded presentations to groundbreaking debuts, the runway offered dynamic energy and endless inspiration. Here are the key highlights that defined this year's iconic event. Manish Malhotra Luxury Pret Manish Malhotra kicked off the season with an extraordinary showcase of luxury pret. He blended classic Indian craftsmanship with modern contemporary silhouettes. The collection featured sharp cuts, fluid draped skirts, and tailored jackets. Glittering sequins and intricate threadwork caught the spotlight. Models, as well as the showstoppers Sara Ali Khan and Ayushmann Khurrana, glided down the runway in versatile pieces. Celebrities filled the front row, adding extra glamour to the presentation. Anushree Reddy Presents Maya Anushree Reddy teamed up with Lakme Salon to present her captivating collection, Maya . Soft pastels, delicate embroidery, and flowing organzas dominated the runway. Reddy focused on lightweight bridal couture and breezy festive pieces. Her layered skirts and intricate floral motifs captivated the audience immediately. Sara Arjun looked stunning in one of the outfits as she walked down the runway. The presentation offered total visual harmony between beauty and fashion. Every look delivered a fresh perspective on traditional festive wear. Attendees left with endless inspiration for the upcoming celebration season. Richa Khemka and Gaurav Jagtiani The NEXA Spotlight initiative brought fresh creative vision to the runway under the theme 'The Unseen' . Winning designers Linetribe by Gaurav Jagtiani and Richa Khemka shared the stage to present two distinct interpretations. Richa Khemka presented Vesper , exploring light, shadow, and evolving identity through sculptural silhouettes, laser-cut textures, and striking metallic accents. Actress Diana Penty made an appearance, closing the showcase with immense poise. Linetribe introduced Pinnacle , featuring structured tailoring, sharp outerwear, and hand-executed quilting. Both collections drew praise for their technical craftsmanship and emotive storytelling. Grand Finale: AM:IT by Amit Aggarwal Amit Aggarwal delivered a spectacular closing performance with his label, AM:IT. He transformed the runway into a futuristic landscape driven by architecture and sustainable design. Aggarwal utilised recycled polymers, metallic cords, and structured textiles to create dynamic forms. His signature wave patterns and sharp geometric lines redefined modern haute couture. The creations moved like living sculptures under dramatic lighting displays. Bold colours lit up the stage. Aggarwal successfully fused industrial innovation with fine handcrafting techniques. Aneet Padda commanded the stage in an avant-garde outfit that stole the entire show. Audiences cheered as the grand finale concluded on a triumphantly high note. A New Era of Style The 2026 October edition of Lakme Fashion Week x FDCI redefined contemporary style standards across the board. Designers successfully balanced traditional Indian heritage with bold futuristic vision. The runway delivered unforgettable creativity and flair. This season clearly proved that Indian fashion continues to innovate, inspire, and lead on a global scale. He began his career in 1990 as a Bollywood costume designer, launched his eponymous label in 2005 and is best known for glamorous bridal lehengas, sequinned sarees and dressing India’s biggest film stars. In 2026 he debuted at Paris Haute Couture Week and launched Menswear Luxe Prêt at Lakmé Fashion Week. For more than 35 years, he has dressed Bollywood’s biggest stars, designed some of India’s most-watched weddings and helped define what Indian glamour looks like on screen and off it. This guide covers his early life, film career, awards, signature style, iconic lehengas and sarees, celebrity weddings, global milestones, and where to find his designs today. Key Takeaways He started as a Bollywood costume designer in 1990 with the film Swarg. He won the Filmfare Award for Best Costume Design for Rangeela (1995). He launched his eponymous label in 2005, covering bridal couture, prêt, menswear, high jewellery and beauty. His signature style combines sequins, fluid chiffons, pastels and ombrés, and heritage crafts like chikankari and Kashmiri embroidery. In 2026 he closed Dubai Fashion Week, debuted at Paris Haute Couture Week and returned to Lakmé Fashion Week. Manish Malhotra prêt is available at six Aza Fashions stores. Manish Malhotra at a Glance Born: 5 December 1966, Mumbai, India Education: Elphinstone College, Mumbai Profession: Fashion designer, couturier, costume designer, film producer Career began: 1990, costume design for Swarg Label launched: 2005 Major award: Filmfare Award for Best Costume Design, Rangeela Known for: Bridal lehengas, sequinned sarees, Bollywood costumes Ventures: Couture, prêt, menswear, high jewellery, beauty, Stage5 Production Flagship cities: Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Dubai Who Is Manish Malhotra? Manish Malhotra is one of India’s most celebrated fashion designers and the founder of his eponymous fashion house. He is known as Bollywood’s favourite couturier, having designed costumes for hundreds of Hindi films and wedding outfits for many of India’s leading actors. His work spans film costume design, bridal couture, ready-to-wear, menswear, high jewellery, beauty and film production. He is also an advocate for Indian handcrafts, particularly chikankari and Kashmiri embroidery. What Is Manish Malhotra Known For? Manish Malhotra is known for five things: Bollywood costume design: iconic looks in films like Rangeela, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham… and Om Shanti Om Bridal lehengas: embellished pastel, ombré and jewel-toned lehengas worn by celebrity brides Sequinned sarees: the shimmering party saree, popularised by the “Desi Girl” look in Dostana Celebrity weddings: including Kiara Advani and Sidharth Malhotra’s 2023 wedding Global Indian couture: shows at Dubai Fashion Week and Paris Haute Couture Week Manish Malhotra’s Early Life and Education Manish Malhotra was born on 5 December 1966 in Mumbai and studied at Elphinstone College. He had no formal training in fashion design. He worked briefly as a model, and a lifelong love of Hindi cinema pulled him towards the film sets where he would build his career. That outsider beginning shaped his approach. Instead of studying fashion in a classroom, he learned it through character, camera and colour. Those lessons still define his work. How Manish Malhotra Changed Bollywood Costume Design Manish Malhotra made film costumes a storytelling tool, designing outfits that were character-driven and trend-setting at the same time. Before him, costumes in Hindi cinema were often an afterthought. His first major project was styling Juhi Chawla for Swarg in 1990. Urmila Matondkar’s wardrobe in Rangeela (1995) was the turning point. It earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Costume Design and made him the most in-demand costume designer in the industry. Manish Malhotra’s Iconic Films and Looks Rangeela (1995): Urmila Matondkar’s bold, modern wardrobe Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995): Kajol’s wardrobe, including the famous green lehenga Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998): Kajol’s and Rani Mukerji’s college and wedding looks Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham… (2001): Kareena Kapoor’s unforgettable “Poo” wardrobe Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003): Preity Zinta’s New York looks Main Hoon Na (2004): Sushmita Sen’s chiffon sarees Om Shanti Om (2007): Retro glamour for Deepika Padukone’s debut Dostana (2008): Priyanka Chopra’s “Desi Girl” sequinned saree Student of the Year (2012): Alia Bhatt’s debut wardrobe Kalank (2019): Period grandeur for an ensemble cast Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani (2023): Alia Bhatt’s chiffon sarees His film work also crossed borders. He designed for Reese Witherspoon in Vanity Fair (2004) and for Aishwarya Rai Bachchan in the Tamil blockbuster Enthiran (2010). The chiffon saree is perhaps his biggest gift to popular culture. Brides and wedding guests still recreate these looks, and you can explore modern takes in our edit of designer sarees for wedding . What Awards Has Manish Malhotra Won? Manish Malhotra has won the Filmfare Award, multiple IIFA Awards and the Zee Cine Award for costume design. His major honours include: Filmfare Award for Best Costume Design for Rangeela IIFA Awards for Best Costume for Mohabbatein (2001), Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham… (2002) and Kal Ho Naa Ho (2004) Filmfare Award South for Costume Design for Enthiran (2010) Zee Cine Award for Best Costume for Mohabbatein Bollywood Awards Designer of the Year for Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham…, Veer-Zaara and Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna Priyadarshini Memorial Award for his contribution to fashion Iconic Gold Award (2022) for Outstanding Contribution to Bollywood Fashion He has also been named to the BoF 500 and walked the Met Gala red carpet in 2024 and 2025. Think jewel tones, heavier fabrics, and silhouettes that hold their own against string lights and sangeet dance floors. The usual lehenga feels almost too easy. Diana Penty just proved there's a better option. Her latest look, a henna green saree by Mahima Mahajan , is quietly reshaping what winter wedding outfits can look like. It's elegant without trying too hard. It's unexpected without feeling like a costume. And it might just be the push you need to rethink your own wedding season wardrobe. Here's what makes this saree worth talking about. The Henna Green Saree That Sets the Mood Diana Penty in a Mahima Mahajan saree is a masterclass in restraint done right. The piece in question is the SAYARI Saree , rendered in a deep henna green that reads as rich, not loud. It's pre-draped, which means no last-minute pleating panic before the ceremony starts. The fabric pairing does the heavy lifting here: silk organza meets silk velvet, giving the saree both structure and softness in the same breath. This combination is exactly why the look works so well for colder months. Organza brings movement. Velvet brings warmth and weight. Together, they create a saree that feels suited to candlelit mandaps and evening receptions alike. The Craftsmanship That Makes It Special Look closer and the details start doing the talking. The pallu carries intricate embroidery, the kind that catches light as you move. It's not overdone. It's placed with intention. Then there's the blouse. A richly embellished velvet corset blouse anchors the whole look. It's structured, a little bit sharp, and entirely modern. The embroidery adds texture and depth across the saree. The corset blouse adds edge. Put together, they turn a traditional drape into something that feels current. This is Indian craftsmanship speaking a contemporary language. Why This Saree Works for Winter Weddings Winter wedding guest looks tend to lean into richer colors for a reason. Jewel tones photograph beautifully against the season's muted light, and they hold their own indoors under warm lighting too. Velvet accents matter here as well. They add a tactile richness that chiffon or georgette simply can't replicate in cooler months. Detailed embroidery and statement silhouettes round out the formula, giving outfits enough presence to stand up to the formality of wedding events. A pre-draped saree, like Diana Penty's henna green pick, offers all of this without the commitment of a full lehenga set. It's a strong alternative for cocktail nights, sangeet functions, and receptions. It moves easily, photographs well, and still feels like an occasion outfit. For anyone attending multiple wedding events this season, a corset blouse saree like this one is worth considering. It bridges the gap between traditional and modern, without asking you to choose one over the other. How to Style a Corset Saree for Wedding Season A saree with this much detail doesn't need extra noise around it. If you're building a similar look, let the outfit lead. Statement earring s work well against a plain neckline, especially when the blouse itself is already embellished. A sleek bun keeps the focus on the pallu and embroidery instead of competing with it. For makeup, softly defined eyes and luminous skin tend to complement richer fabrics like velvet. A bold lip can be the final note, adding a bit of edge without overwhelming the outfit. These are simply ideas to consider when styling a corset saree for your own wedding season plans. Keep accessories minimal elsewhere. When the blouse and pallu already make a statement, less really is more. The Modern Appeal of Mahima Mahajan's Design Mahima Mahajan has built a reputation for designs that sit at the intersection of heritage and modernity. The SAYARI Saree is part of her FIZA collection , where traditional techniques meet contemporary silhouettes like the corset blouse. This approach reflects where winter wedding fashion is heading. Brides and guests alike are moving away from predictable choices, favoring pieces that feel personal and considered instead. A pre-draped saree with a structured blouse captures that shift perfectly. It respects tradition while still feeling like it belongs to today's charm. A Strong Case for the Statement Saree This Wedding Season Diana Penty's henna green saree isn't just a styling moment. It's a reminder that wedding dressing doesn't have to follow the same script every time. A well-made saree, paired with the right blouse and a few thoughtful details, can hold its own against any lehenga. If you've got a winter wedding calendar ahead, let this look be your sign to reach for something different. A travel enthusiast at heart, she's always chasing new trends and destinations. Outside of work, you’ll likely find her at the gym or unwinding with a good movie. It arrives, it commands, and it stays in the photographs for decades. But no two reds are alike. One designer’s red is a smouldering, sindoor-deep heirloom shade, another’s is a sun-warmed vermilion, and a third is a rebellious tomato-pop that makes the mandap look underdressed. Choosing a red bridal lehenga is really choosing a point of view: Mughal grandeur, Rajasthani craft, Bollywood glamour or quiet, textile-led heritage. Here are fifteen designers who each speak red in their own dialect. 1. Sabyasachi: The Red That Became a Category Sabyasachi ’s red is practically its own Pantone: deep, lived-in, almost antique. Rooted in Bengal’s textile heritage, his lehengas layer Banarasi weaves, hand embroidery and a sense of storied nostalgia. The USP is emotion: the bride looks like she belongs to a family history. It’s the benchmark for heirloom bridal, and a status symbol in its own right. A Sabyasachi bride is a story of her own. Visit select Aza Fashions stores to experience his signature bridal creations in person. 2. Manish Malhotra: Bollywood’s Red Carpet, Bridal Edition Manish Malhotra defined the film-star bride, and his red lehengas carry that cinematic shimmer. Expect sequins, intricate zardozi and flattering cuts that photograph like a movie still. His USP is glamour with a guarantee: celebrity-endorsed, camera-ready and unabashedly showstopping. He’s the choice for brides who want to feel like the lead in their own love story. Make your Manish Malhotra moment a reality. Visit select Aza Fashions stores to experience his bridal creations firsthand. 3. Ritu Kumar: The Textile Historian in Red Ritu Kumar has shaped Indian fashion since the 1960s, and her bridal red is rooted in craft memory. Think Banarasi brocades, zardozi, and motifs drawn from Mughal and regional archives. Her USP is heritage with credibility: a red that feels like it was passed down rather than purchased. It suits traditional brides who love textile story over trend. 4. Rimple and Harpreet Narula: Couture with Edges Delhi duo Rimple and Harpreet Narula brings architectural thinking to bridal wear, with dramatic cuts, sculpted silhouettes and exquisitely detailed embellishment. Their reds feel regal and a little theatrical, closer to couture than convention. The USP is distinct design language, for the bride who wants her lehenga to look like nobody else’s. 5. Masaba: The Rule-Bending Red Masaba Gupta ’s world is bold, playful and gleefully modern. Where other designers lean traditional, her approach to red trades in colour-play, graphic energy and a youthful attitude. The USP is personality: for the bride who wants her wedding look to feel like an extension of her own quirky, confident style. 6. Mrunalini Rao: South-Meets-Couture Craftsmanship Hyderabad-based Mrunalini Rao brings meticulous handwork and a distinctly rich, layered approach to bridal wear. Her red lehengas reward a close look, with dense embroidery and artisanal depth. The USP is craft intensity, for brides who want their lehenga to feel deeply made. 7. Ridhi Mehra: Romance, Hand-Stitched Ridhi Mehra ’s Delhi label leans soft-focus and dreamy, with detailed embroidery and fluid silhouettes that move beautifully. Her reds feel romantic, not rigid, often paired with delicate florals and tonal work. The USP is a modern, feminine take on tradition, for brides who want to look luminous rather than armoured. 8. Dolly J: The Drape Whisperer Dolly J is known for reimagining how a lehenga is worn, with sari-style drapes, capes and structured layers. Her red bridal pieces play with silhouette as much as surface, giving brides something more fluid and unexpected. The USP is innovation: a lehenga that feels like a styled look rather than a conventional set. 9. Sheetal Batra: The Quiet Perfectionist Sheetal Batra ’s Delhi label is built on restraint and finish. Her red lehengas favour refined zardozi, pearl and sequin work over sheer volume, and the embroidery sits like jewellery on the fabric. Her USP is polish: cuts that flatter, balanced embellishment, and a red that feels elegant rather than loud. She’s a safe harbour for brides who want grace without shouting. 10. Seema Gujral: The Maximalist Queen of Delhi Seema Gujral is a veteran of Delhi’s bridal circuit, and her aesthetic is drama in capital letters. Her red lehengas are often dense with Mughal-inspired motifs, heavy zari and regal volume, made for a grand entrance. She’s popular with brides who want the full ceremonial spectacle, where the lehenga does as much talking as the families. 11. Torani: Jaipur in a Lehenga Torani brings Rajasthani soul to the bridal wardrobe, with gota patti, bandhani-inspired detail and a lighter, more wearable feel. Its reds feel festive and joyful, closer to a vibrant Jaipur celebration than a heavy museum piece. The USP is craft-forward charm, often at a gentler weight, ideal for brides who plan to dance through their own sangeet. 12. Azeera: Modern Opulence, Unapologetically Azeera speaks to the bride who wants her lehenga to read as luxury from across the room. Think richly layered embellishment, contemporary silhouettes and a festive, jewel-box sensibility. Its reds lean glamorous and statement-making, designed for brides who see their wedding as a fashion moment as much as a ritual. 13. Nitika Gujral: Tradition with a Contemporary Pulse Nitika Gujral balances rich embroidery with silhouettes that feel current and wearable. Her bridal reds suit the bride who respects the classics but wants a fresher proportion, a lighter dupatta or a more modern cut. The USP is versatility: a lehenga that honours the ritual while feeling right for today’s wedding calendar. 14. Angad Singh: Regal, Refined, Rooted Angad Singh ’s design language leans regal and polished, with traditional sensibilities and a clean, confident finish. His reds suit the bride who wants a classic bridal presence without excess. The USP is quiet authority: a lehenga that looks timeless in photographs for years to come. 15. Jigar and Nikita: Colour with a Wedding-Day Glow Jigar and Nikita are known for lehengas that feel celebratory and richly worked, with a bright, festive sensibility. Their reds tend toward the vibrant, paired with detailed embroidery that catches the light on the dance floor. The USP is joyful wearability: a bridal look that feels as happy as the occasion. Name * Email ID * Contact No * Message Captcha * Home Aza Magazine Fashion and Style Designer Wedding How To SHOP Cover Stories Visual Stories × https://www.youtube.com/embed?v=YEtmEUDfWBE?rel=0&showinfo=0 × https://www.youtube.com/embed/fDlWjeJ3Elo?rel=0&showinfo=0 × https://www.youtube.com/embed/s5-rRn7C5hM?rel=0&showinfo=0 × https://www.youtube.com/embed/oG4Kvqk7yws?rel=0&showinfo=0 × https://www.youtube.com/embed/lB4ULZoU3z0?rel=0&showinfo=0 × https://www.youtube.com/embed/ukEg2_t6AXo?rel=0&showinfo=0 Home Accessories How to Style a Red Saree for Karwa Chauth 2026 Like the Moon Is Watching Accessories Festive Styles How To How to Style a Red Saree for Karwa Chauth 2026 Like the Moon Is Watching October 17, 2026 Red is not just a colour on Karwa Chauth. It is a mood, a memory and a statement of intent. It’s the shade of bridal lehengas folded away in trunks, of mehndi still staining the palms, of a long day of devotion that ends with a sieve, a diya and a very patient moon. A red saree is the one outfit that carries all of that at once. The real question is how to wear it so you look like yourself, only more luminous. Pick Your Red Like You Pick Your Mood Not all reds are equal. Tomato and vermilion read festive and sunlit. Deep cherry and oxblood turn dramatic after dark, and brick or rust feels modern and earthy. If you’ll be photographed under warm diyas, go for reds with a hint of orange. If the evening is mostly fairy lights and flash photography, jewel-toned crimsons hold their depth better. Then look at the fabric. Silk organza and tissue catch the diya glow and look beautiful in motion. Banarasi and kanjeevaram say tradition. Georgette and chiffon are for those who want to eat the post-fast thali in comfort. The Blouse Is the Plot Twist A red saree is already doing the talking, so let the blouse bring the surprise. Gold zardozi or a mirror-work blouse is a safe, glowing choice. A contrast blouse in ivory, blush or antique gold makes a classic six yards look fresh. If your saree is heavily embroidered, keep the blouse sleek with a deep V, a boat neck or elbow-length sleeves. Drape It Like You Mean It The drape sets the silhouette. The classic Nivi with crisp pleats is timeless and photographs well. A Bengali-style drape with the pallu over the shoulder and the keys tucked in is nostalgic and regal. For something more modern, try a belted pallu, a half-pleated pre-stitched drape or a cape-style pallu. Pin the pleats securely. You’ll be sitting, standing, circling a thali and climbing terraces, so the drape should survive all of it. Jewellery: Let the Gold Do the Talking Red and gold have been a power couple for centuries. If your saree is rich and embroidered, choose one hero piece, like a statement choker or a layered temple necklace . If the saree is simple, go all out with a kundan or polki set, jhumkas and a maang tikka. Polki and kundan glow beautifully against red. Temple jewellery brings a South Indian grace, and pearls soften the intensity if you want something quieter. Don’t forget a nath, which is trending for festive looks. The Accessory Edit: The Little Things That Finish the Look Karwa Chauth accessories are loaded with meaning, so choose with care. Stack a set of red and gold bangles on both wrists, and add a cocktail ring or a kada if you want the mix-and-match look. A small potli bag holds your phone, lipstick and a few hairpins. A sindoor-red bindi, ideally a bold round one, completes the face. Finish with embroidered juttis or block-heel sandals. You’ll be on your feet all evening. Hair That Frames the Face and the Moon Your hairstyle should balance the weight of the jewellery. Soft curls with a side parting and a flower tucked behind the ear are romantic and easy. A sleek low bun with a gajra says old-world glamour, especially with a maang tikka . A braided half-up style with pearls or small jewelled pins works for a modern-festive look. If you’re wearing a heavy choker, go for an updo that shows off your neck. Fresh jasmine or rose gajras give the look fragrance as well as style. Beauty: The Glow That Survives the Fast You’ve gone a day without food and water, so skin prep matters. Start with a hydrating primer and a dewy base so your face doesn’t look flat under camera flash. Add a touch of highlighter on the cheekbones and the inner corners of the eyes. For eyes, a smoky kohl rim with soft gold or bronze lids flatters almost every skin tone. For lips, a classic brick red or deep rose is timeless, while a berry shade adds drama. Finish with sindoor and a set of mehndi-darkened hands, and you’re done. The Last Look Before the Moon Rises Before you step out, do a quick mirror check. Is the pallu pinned? Are the bangles settled? Is the lipstick still on? Carry a small touch-up kit and a pocket mirror for the moonrise rush. Whatever you wear, the best accessory is the way you carry it, with a bit of mischief, a lot of love and the confidence of someone who has fasted all day and still looks this good. It’s the season to turn heads together, colour-coordinate without looking too matchy-matchy and start traditions that are yours alone. Think jewel-toned outfits, dreamy pastels, rich fabrics and statement-making silhouettes that bring the festive magic without repeating your wedding-day looks. Whether you’re drawn to the timeless charm of red and ivory, the allure of emerald green or the playful shimmer of mirror work, these outfit pairings will make your first Diwali together one to remember. 12 Diwali Outfit Combinations for Couples Who Love to Coordinate Your first Diwali as newlyweds deserves outfits that are every bit as special as the occasion. From colour-coordinated classics to statement-making festive ensembles, these 12 looks strike the perfect balance between romance, tradition and personal style. 1. The Classic Red and Ivory Combination Nothing feels quite as timeless as red and ivory for a newlywed couple's first Diwali. She can wear the border embroidered saree set, styled with gold jewellery and a sleek bun. He can complement her look with the Nehru jacket and kurta set The combination brings together traditional charm and coordinated festive dressing without looking too matchy-matchy. 2. Champagne Gold, Head to Toe For couples who love a little festive glamour, champagne gold is a beautiful alternative to traditional reds and maroons. She can make an entrance in the geometric and floral pattern lehenga Set, pairing its gold-toned look with delicate earrings and a statement ring . He can complement her in the beige patterned sherwani and pant set. Together, the understated neutrals and festive embellishments create a polished look for Diwali parties and family celebrations. 3. Matching Jewel Tones Emerald green brings a rich, celebratory mood to Diwali dressing, especially when paired with velvet and intricate embroidery. She can opt for the Draped Saree with Corset, a contemporary take on traditional draping. He can match the mood with the Hand-Embroidered Velvet Bandhgala . The combination feels regal and coordinated, making it ideal for an evening celebration or a dressed-up family gathering. 4. Pastel Romance Not every festive look needs to be bold or heavily embellished. Pastels bring a softer, romantic touch to a couple's first Diwali together. She can wear the Blush Embroidered Silk Lehenga Set, styled with pearl jewellery or delicate kundan accents. He can complement the blush tones with the Embroidered Jacket and Kurta Set. This pairing works beautifully for daytime pujas, intimate dinners and celebrations where understated elegance is the mood. 5. The Modern Maharaja Look For a Diwali party that calls for a little drama, combine contemporary silhouettes with regal detailing. She can choose the Embroidered Corset Lehenga Set, adding statement earrings and a sleek hairstyle to let the silhouette shine. He can bring his own dose of grandeur with the Blue Velvet Floral Embroidered Achkan. The structured corset and rich velvet create a striking contrast, perfect for newlyweds attending an upscale Diwali soirée. 6. Banarasi Meets Brocade Traditional craftsmanship deserves a place in your first Diwali wardrobe. While a Banarasi saree or brocade lehenga is a classic choice, you can also introduce heritage-inspired richness through embroidered festive separates. She can wear the Mustard Patch Silk Kurta Gharara Set, accessorised with gold jhumkas and traditional bangles. He can complement the look with the Nehru Jacket Kurta Set. The warm tones and classic silhouettes make this pairing especially suited to a family Lakshmi Puja or a festive dinner with elders. 7. Contemporary Saree and Textured Kurta For couples hosting friends at home or attending a relaxed Diwali get-together, contemporary silhouettes offer the right balance of comfort and occasionwear appeal. She can wear the Pink Pre-Draped Lehenga Saree, which combines the elegance of a saree with the ease of a pre-draped silhouette. He can pair it with the mirror-embroidered chanderi embroidered kurta set and neutral combination feels modern, making it perfect for hosting friends or celebrating at home. How Newlyweds Can Coordinate Their Diwali Outfits Match colours, not entire outfits. If she wears emerald, he can choose ivory with a green pocket square or a coordinating green jacket. Balance the embellishment. If her outfit features intricate embroidery or sequins, his can be more restrained, with one standout detail. Dress for the occasion. Silk sarees and kurta sets work beautifully for puja, while corsets, velvet and contemporary silhouettes are ideal for evening parties. Bring wedding jewellery back into rotation. Style a bridal necklace with a simpler saree or pair statement earrings with a minimal lehenga. Invest in versatile pieces. A textured Nehru jacket, silk kurta, versatile saree or neutral lehenga can be restyled for weddings and future festive occasions. Coordinate the finishing touches. Complementary footwear, matching metallic accents and coordinated accessories can bring two outfits together without making them look overly planned. The best outfit idea for a newlywed Diwali is one that feels like you, individually and as a couple. Choose a traditional silk or embroidered look, pair it with a complementary kurta or bandhgala, and introduce one shared colour or metallic accent. Whether you opt for regal jewel tones, romantic pastels or contemporary festive silhouettes, your first Diwali together is the perfect occasion to create a style tradition of your own. Whether you're a bride, bridesmaid, or stylish guest attending a destination wedding in the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, or UAE, Fabilicious brings you a curated selection of designer Indo-Western sets that match every vibe. Let’s break it down by function and show you how to stand out at every event. Bridal Welcome Party: Luxe Looks That Set the Tone Whether you're the bride hosting an intimate welcome soirée or attending one as a guest, these Indo-Western gowns are all about first impressions with finesse. White Pearl Embroidered Gown This ethereal pearl gown is a standout choice for a bridal welcome party , especially in resort or destination settings. Pastel Yellow Embroidered Gown Fresh, romantic, and soft—ideal for daytime events or your welcome brunch with the bridesmaids. Style Tip: Keep accessories minimal—let the embroidery shine. Add pearl studs or a sleek clutch for a complete look. 💍 Roka Ready: Understated Elegance Meets Modern Tailoring Roka is often the first official event, and your outfit should be elegant yet refined. Go for clean silhouettes with subtle mirrorwork for a fresh first impression. Beige & Silver Mirrorwork Pant Set with Long Blazer This sleek beige blazer set is ideal for a sophisticated roka ceremony—pair it with nude heels and delicate diamond studs for a polished finish. Ivory Co-ord Set with Multicolour Mirrorwork Cape The ivory and multicolour cape adds just the right amount of festive flair while keeping things soft and breathable. 🌿 Mehendi Mood: Bright, Comfortable & Insta-Ready Mehendi calls for outfits that are playful, vibrant, and comfortable—especially if you'll be dancing or getting henna done. Lime Green Silk Pant Set with Cape With its flowy cape and sunny hue, this silk set is a dream for daytime mehendi celebrations. Purple Embroidered Kaftan Set with Palazzo Lightweight and fuss-free, this kaftan set blends comfort with ethnic flair—ideal for outdoor mehendis or poolside celebrations. 💃 Sangeet Showstoppers: Glamorous, Comfortable & Ready to Dance For your sangeet night, go bold with silhouettes that shimmer and allow movement—co-ord sets, jackets, and glam detailing are key. Black Embroidered Co-ord Set This black set is chic and powerful—pair with bold earrings and high heels to own the dance floor. Blue Mirrorwork Co-ord Set with Blazer A mix of print and mirror makes this a statement Indo-Western outfit for bridesmaids or the bride's sister. 🌍 Why Global Clients Trust Fabilicious At Fabilicious, we make it easy for clients in the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, and UAE to shop new Indo-Western outfits online with: ✅ Latest drops from top Indian designers ✅ Made-to-measure fittings with our “MySize” service ✅ EU-friendly return policy ✅ Complimentary virtual style consultations Celebrate every wedding function in style with Fabilicious. The weeks leading up to Diwali bring a flurry of decisions: which outfit for the puja, which look for the party, which colour this year. This guide covers everything you need to put together the perfect Diwali ethnic wear looks for 2026. What to Wear for Diwali: The Basics Colour matters. Traditional Diwali colours include deep reds, royal blues, emerald greens, mustard yellows, and gold. Fabric sets the occasion. Puja calls for something graceful and traditional; the evening party invites more drama and shine. Comfort is non-negotiable. You will be sitting, standing, lighting diyas, eating, so your outfit needs to move with you. Diwali Outfit Ideas for 2026 1. The Embroidered Suit Set A classic for a reason. An embroidered suit set in jewel tones, deep wine, midnight blue, or emerald green, hits the sweet spot between traditional and refined. Pair with statement jhumkas and a potli bag. Shop our Festive Wear collection . 2. The Farshi Salwar Set The farshi salwar's floor-sweeping hem creates instant drama without requiring heavy embellishment. Opt for an ombre farshi in dusty rose or burnt orange for a modern Diwali look that photographs beautifully. 3. The Co-Ord Set in Festive Colours For Diwali parties and friends' gatherings, a festive co-ord set in rich brocade or printed fabric is effortlessly chic. Browse Co-Ord Sets . 4. The Cape Set A cape jacket set layered over a matching kurta and pant is the Diwali party outfit of the moment. The cape adds drama, the co-ordinated base keeps it grounded. 5. The Kaani Suit Set For those who want something deeply rooted in Indian craft traditions, a Kaani jacquard suit set is unmatched. Shop Kaani Suit Sets . Shop Our Diwali Bestsellers Black Shirt with Brocade Pants Shop Now Navy Blue Crush Suit with Chanderi Dupatta Shop Now Wine Velvet Suit with Tulip Pants Shop Now Diwali Outfit Colours to Watch in 2026 Burgundy and wine: Rich, traditional, always right for Diwali Forest green and emerald: Fresh and festive, pairs beautifully with gold jewellery Dusty rose and blush: Soft and elegant for day events and puja Ivory and cream: Understated luxury, especially beautiful in embroidered fabrics Midnight blue: A modern alternative to black for evening Diwali parties Diwali Jewellery and Styling Tips Chandelier earrings or jhumkas work with almost every ethnic silhouette A potli bag in coordinating fabric elevates any outfit Keep your dupatta draped loosely for comfort, or opt for a set that does not require one Block heels or juttis are more practical and just as stylish as stilettos for a long Diwali evening Shop our full Diwali Festive Collection and find your perfect Diwali look. While traditional wear is always a beautiful choice, there’s a fresh trend on the rise— Indo-Western outfits . These striking ensembles perfectly blend Eastern elegance and Western chic, giving you the best of both worlds. Gone are the days when Diwali meant sticking to only traditional lehengas or sarees. Today’s fashion scene allows you to experiment, combine, and redefine festive wear. So, why not step out of your comfort zone this Diwali and explore the world of Indo-Western outfits for women ? Co-ord sets have become immensely popular for their easy-to-wear yet fashionable appeal. This ensemble features a matching top and wide-legged trousers, offering comfort and sophistication. The beauty of this Indo-Western outfit lies in its simplicity. The tailored cut of the trousers balances the flowy top, creating a streamlined, effortlessly chic look. Perfect for Diwali parties or family gatherings, the bright red hue immediately adds a festive flair, while the minimalistic design ensures you remain comfortable throughout the night. The fitted corset-style bodice beautifully complements the flowing skirt, creating a glamorous yet refined look perfect for evening events. Corset-inspired outfits have been dominating the designer Indo-Western outfit scene, and for a good reason—they highlight your figure while adding an element of drama to your ensemble. This deep burgundy piece is ideal for women who want to step out in something unique yet festive. Styling Tip : With this outfit, keep accessories minimal since the corset adds plenty of detail. The standout feature of this outfit is its detailed embroidery, which adds a touch of grandeur without going overboard. The sharara’s flared pants allow for easy movement, whether you’re dancing at a Diwali party or performing a traditional puja. Styling Tip : To complete the festive look, pair this outfit with bold gold jewellery and strappy sandals. Styling Tip : To balance the contemporary silhouette, go for chunky, traditional jewellery like jhumkas or a statement necklace. Add a pair of juttis or block heels to keep the look rooted in traditional aesthetics while maintaining comfort. 5. The floaty organza adds a romantic touch to the ensemble, while the embroidered kurta keeps things festive and elegant. Designer Fashion | Aashni + Co About Aashni + Co Founded in London in 2012, Aashni + Co began with a boutique in Notting Hill, becoming one of the earliest destinations outside India, in our experience, to champion authenticated creations from the country's most celebrated designers, including Sabyasachi . Today, the luxury platform curates a portfolio of, by our own count, over 100 leading Indian fashion houses, serving a global clientele across the UK, India, the UAE, the US, Canada, Australia, Singapore and Europe. Defined by a commitment to authenticity and craftsmanship, every designer featured on Aashni + Co is personally vetted, with each purchase accompanied by a designer-issued invoice. Complementing its curated offering is a bespoke styling service, available through private consultations in London and Mumbai, as well as virtual appointments for clients worldwide, delivering a seamless and highly personalised luxury shopping experience. Luxury Indian fashion is not a single thing Luxury Indian fashion is not a single thing. It is a world of extraordinary range from Sabyasachi's heritage bridal lehengas, hand-embroidered over thousands of hours, to Torani 's joyful printed separates designed for effortless everyday dressing, to Gaurav Gupta 's sculptural gowns seen on red carpets from Mumbai to Los Angeles. What connects these designers is not a single occasion, aesthetic or customer. What connects them is craftsmanship, intention and the understanding that clothing carries meaning. This guide is an introduction to that world shaped by experience, not simply a catalogue. Whether you are investing ₹25,000 or ₹10 lakh, whether you are shopping from London, Dubai, New York or Mumbai and whether you are dressing for your wedding, a celebration or an intimate dinner, what follows is a clear and practical perspective on luxury Indian designer fashion and the designers defining it today. What makes luxury Indian designer fashion worth the investment? Luxury Indian designer fashion is worth the investment because it offers a level of craftsmanship, quality and artistry that goes far beyond the garment itself. The true value lies not in a famous label, but in the skill, time and expertise behind its creation. A Sabyasachi bridal lehenga, for instance, may require over a thousand hours of hand embroidery by master artisans, while an Anamika Khanna ensemble can bring together multiple regional weaving and craft traditions within a single silhouette. The most important distinction is between craft-led luxury and name-led luxury. Craft-led luxury is built on exceptional materials, specialised handwork, thoughtful construction and techniques passed down through generations. Every detail, from the fabric and embroidery to the fit and finish, is created with intention. Name-led luxury, on the other hand, often relies on brand recognition while incorporating production shortcuts that may not be immediately visible but become apparent over time. Luxury designer pieces also hold their value in ways that fast fashion and mass-produced occasion wear cannot. They offer superior craftsmanship, timeless appeal, emotional significance and often become garments that are treasured, preserved and passed down. Before making a significant investment, it is worth asking three simple questions: Is the embroidery hand-crafted or machine-made? What is the fabric and where was it woven? How long did the garment take to create? The answers reveal far more about a piece's true value than any designer name ever can. "When you let craft thrive, you not only restore economic sustainability but also the pride and dignity of workmanship and artisanal skill. It is through the consumption of craft that you encourage the continuity of our legacy." — Sabyasachi Mukherjee Source: Sabyasachi Official — Heritage Weddings . How do you choo
